cim: Franco Oblatore Presents "The Millennial Musical Showdown: AI vs. HI" A Global Music Challenge Calling for a Human Dialogue About Artificial Intelligence
cim_eredeti: Franco Oblatore Presents "The Millennial Musical Showdown: AI vs. HI" A Global Music Challenge Calling for a Human Dialogue About Artificial Intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
AZZATE, IT / ACCESS Newswire / October 21, 2026 / Franco Oblatore, Italian classical pianist, music creator and founder of Francoobla Music, has presented "The Millennial Musical Showdown: AI vs. HI (Artificial Intelligence vs. Human Intelligence)," a proposed global musical and entertainment format designed to bring artificial intelligence and human intelligence together through a friendly cultural challenge.

After decades of experience in music, Oblatore developed the concept around a broader question: how can society approach artificial intelligence not only through technology, investment and business, but also through music, creativity and human interaction?

Oblatore's central message behind the proposed challenge is that the rapid development of artificial intelligence should encourage an open, friendly and above all human dialogue about the technology and its relationship with society.

In his words, the project is intended to encourage a conversation about AI that goes beyond discussions of trillions of dollars in investment and focuses instead on how artificial intelligence can become a useful tool and a positive part of human life.

"With AI = Artificial Intelligence, we must open an open, friendly, and above all human dialogue - and not just talk about trillions in investments. This is the true reason behind the challenge I have proposed to a pool of 6.2 billion people," said Oblatore.

The proposed AI vs. HI format is intended to create that dialogue through music. Rather than presenting artificial intelligence and human intelligence as opposing forces, the project explores how the two can work together, with AI serving as a technological and creative assistant while human knowledge, experience and artistic direction remain central.

Oblatore, who has approximately six decades of experience as a classical pianist, describes the development of AI-assisted music as part of a longer history of technological change in music. Electronic organs, electric guitars, synthesizers, microphones, mixers, amplifiers, recording systems and post-production technologies have all changed how music is created and experienced.

The proposed challenge therefore asks audiences to consider AI-assisted music within this continuing technological evolution.

The format is intended to reach a broad international audience and is being presented for potential development with television networks, streaming platforms, entertainment companies and production partners, particularly in the United States.

The project is not presented as a conventional talent show. Instead, its proposed structure is based on 20 musical tracks - 10 associated with AI and 10 associated with Human Intelligence (HI) - presented under a defined framework designed to establish equal conditions and direct attention toward the music itself.

The proposed challenge is a neutral, nonpolitical and purely cultural music competition involving 20 total tracks - 10 associated with AI and 10 with HI.

Franco Oblatore is identified as the project's informal and voluntary representative for the AI technology side.

The project materials identify Oblatore as rights holder and reference U.S. Copyright Office Case No. 1-15211873131 and SIAE No. 2026/01584.

The format is based on a proposed 50/50 framework, with equal rules and conditions for the AI and HI sides.

The initial concept does not require corporate major-label participation or pay-to-play arrangements.

Oblatore's unreleased work "Sei Ovunque" is identified as the official anthem and symbolic musical work of the project.

AI functions as a creative and technical assistant through digital orchestras, production systems and detailed human prompting.

AI-assisted production remains dependent on human direction, musical knowledge, technical experience and artistic decisions.

Human participants contribute musical heritage, knowledge of styles and traditions, and classical foundations.

Both sides are expected to participate with professional seriousness and strong artistic commitment.

The challenge is intended to evaluate participating music according to the musical and artistic criteria established by the format.

The concept is intended for international development, with potential headquarters and venue decisions remaining subject to the rights holder and applicable agreements.

The foundational structure and core principles may be modified only with authorization from the rights holder.

The competition focuses on tracks selected from the project's official AI master repertoire and corresponding human entries.

Creative materials produced through the format are subject to the ownership and co-ownership arrangements established by the project's rights documentation.

The format is designed to maintain structural and editorial independence from traditional major-label gatekeepers.

Participation requires acceptance of the applicable clauses, conditions and rules established for the format.

Questions concerning fairness, interpretation or format rules are intended to be referred to the designated representative or rights holder.

The project's blueprint and implementation remain subject to the applicable intellectual-property and legal protections.

The project recognizes the central role of digital technology in contemporary music production and consumption.

The format proposes that audiences can respond emotionally to AI-assisted music within the broader history of electronic instruments, recording and studio technology.

AI-assisted tracks are intended to be presented alongside high-quality human studio productions for direct comparison.

The proposed inaugural 2027 edition will focus on female vocals, with a potential subsequent edition focusing on male vocals.

Annual, biennial or festival-based editions would remain subject to decisions by the rights holder and production partners.

The project aims to demonstrate the potential of AI and human intelligence working together as complementary creative forces.

AI is positioned as a technological assistant while the human creator remains responsible for artistic direction and decision-making.

The format is intended for major international entertainment stages and venues, potentially including Madison Square Garden, subject to future arrangements.

Future editions may include cash prizes, financial bonuses or other recognition, subject to future decisions and production arrangements.

Future modifications to the rules remain subject to the rights holder and applicable ownership arrangements.

Oblatore identifies himself as the creator and exclusive rights holder and retains authority regarding future licensing, transfer or acquisition of interests in the format under mutually agreed terms.

The project materials identify Lady Jane as the flagship AI vocalist associated with the concept and describe an unreleased master catalog of approximately 200 produced tracks in five languages.

The materials also identify "You're Everywhere" as the English-language reference to the project's international AI anthem, corresponding to the Italian title "Sei Ovunque."

The catalog and related creative assets are intended to support future development of the format, subject to applicable intellectual-property rights and production arrangements.

Oblatore is presenting AI vs. HI for potential development with U.S. television networks, streaming platforms, entertainment companies and international production partners. Potential development could include television, streaming, festivals and live entertainment, subject to separate production, licensing and commercial agreements.

The broader objective is to create a friendly cultural environment in which audiences can explore the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence, human intelligence and music.
